body:
Client side of protocol versioning (T-240), web and Android: see the design of record. The server
side is T-243 (in parallel; work against the contract, mock the server).

* Both clients: `protocol.ts` / `Protocol.kt` constants = 3; the header on EVERY API request;
  error code `client_outdated` in apiErrors.ts / ErrorText.kt, the wire-contract error table
  is done by T-243 (do not edit docs/wire-contract.md), nine locales, paired by identical English.
* Web: 426 handling exactly as specified (one automatic reload with a sessionStorage guard, then a
  full-page "Update required" notice with Reload; syncing stops). The header goes through
  `apiFetch`; other fetches to the API if any.
* Android: the header via the interceptor chain for every request; ErrorInterceptor maps 426 to
  an `update required` app-wide signal and the API exception; NOT a forced logout, NOT a row
  error; SyncEngine/SyncWorker stop while the state is set and neither quarantine, drop, block
  nor wipe anything; a blocking full-screen "Update required" screen at the root of the UI that
  automatically runs the existing update check (ignoring the auto-check switch and rate limit)
  and offers the download/install the way the existing prompt does; the no-app-available and
  check-failed variants with Retry.
* The protocol-equality test in the web suite (reads server protocol.py and Android Protocol.kt;
  until T-243 lands, the test reads the constant from where T-243 will put it —
  server/src/shoppinglist_server/protocol.py, `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3` — and may be committed
  failing only if that file does not exist yet; better: skip with a clear message when the file
  is absent and note it in your hand-back).
* New strings go in a NEW clearly marked block right after the "sync health" strings (web) and
  after the sync strings (Android) so they do not collide with the ledger work that edits the
  expense strings in parallel.

Tests: web - header present on every request (login, register, sync), 426 -> exactly one reload,
second 426 within five minutes -> notice and no further reload, an unrelated error does not
reload, the notice component; Android - header on every request (MockWebServer), 426 mapping and
no logout event, SyncEngine leaves dirty/blocked rows untouched and stops, the update-required
state and screen with an available update / no update / failing check (follow the Robolectric
pitfalls in AGENTS.md). Each new test must fail when its change is reverted.
title: Protocol versioning, clients: send the header, handle 426 by updating
